prompt:
Take the first reference photograph and change ONE thing in it: the markings
painted on the road.

Everything else stays exactly as it is: the same Berlin street corner from
the same camera position, the same vertical framing, the same deserted
pavement, the same pedestrian traffic light on its grey pole with the upper
round lens glowing an even plain red, the same pale cream facade with its
stone-framed windows, the same black city bicycles along the wall, the same
granite kerb, the same flat overcast daylight.

THE ONE CHANGE is the red bicycle strip at the bottom of the picture: it
holds ONE EVEN WIDTH along its whole length, and it TURNS.

Coming up from the bottom edge of the picture it runs straight toward the
granite kerb, as wide as a bicycle lane. At the kerb it bends to the LEFT
and follows the street, running along beside the kerb and leaving the
picture at its left edge, still exactly as wide there as at the bend. It is
one continuous ribbon of red asphalt with a dashed white line along each of
its two edges, and one white bicycle pictogram painted flat on it below the
bend.

The pedestrian crossing lies to the LEFT of the strip's lower arm: broad
white bars painted on the grey asphalt, the same bars as in the second
reference photograph, running from the kerb toward the bottom edge and
filling the left of the picture. Where the red strip follows the kerb it is
painted over the far end of those white bars, and the two markings cross.

To the RIGHT of the red strip the road is plain grey asphalt, empty of
paint, all the way to the right edge of the picture.
